profile.campus: Iron Mountain Northern Virginia / Manassas campus (142 acres)
profile.reading:
Iron Mountain Incorporated (NYSE: IRM) is a publicly traded REIT headquartered in Portsmouth, New Hampshire, whose core business is physical and digital records management; its data center division was built substantially through a January 2018 acquisition of IO Data Centers, which added facilities in New Jersey, Ohio, and two Arizona sites, not Virginia.

This building, VA-5, is part of Iron Mountain's 142-acre Northern Virginia data center campus in Prince William County. Per the operator's own site, the full campus currently comprises seven operational data centers, with a planned buildout of nine to ten buildings totaling more than 2,000,000 square feet and 400-plus MW of capacity, and Iron Mountain has separately acquired an adjacent 40-acre parcel for two further buildings totaling roughly 150 additional MW. Iron Mountain does not appear to publish its own dedicated VA-5 location page; this registry found none this session.

Aggregator Baxtel, used here as secondary corroboration only, describes VA-5 as the fifth building on the campus: more than 165,000 square feet, built in 2024, with 40 MW of critical load planned on completion across two data halls, and at one point described as set to become Iron Mountain's largest North American facility once complete. Baxtel also gives VA-5's address as 11560 Hayden Road, differing from the 11580 Hayden Road already on file for this row; this registry has not been able to independently reconcile the two addresses against Prince William County property records this session, so both are noted rather than one being silently discarded. No independently verified Uptime Institute tier certificate was located for this building, and the 40 MW figure is recorded as a planned rather than currently confirmed operating capacity.

Iron Mountain trades on the New York Stock Exchange under ticker IRM and files with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission under CIK 0001020569, structured as a real estate investment trust. Records management remains the company's larger, founding business line by facility count; the data center segment is reported separately in Iron Mountain's public filings as a smaller but faster-growing division. Prince William County's rapid data center buildout, of which this Manassas campus is part, has drawn sustained local debate over land use, power demand, and infrastructure planning in recent years, a context relevant to VA-5's continued construction.

Baxtel also lists VA-5's address as 11560 Hayden Rd, differing from and possibly superseding the 11580 Hayden Rd on file; both are recorded rather than one being silently discarded.

Iron Mountain itself was founded in 1951 as Iron Mountain Atomic Storage Corporation by Herman Knaust, a former mushroom entrepreneur who had purchased a depleted iron ore mine near Kingston, New York, went public in 1996, became a real estate investment trust in 2014, and as of 2023 is headquartered in Portsmouth, New Hampshire. The operators own current data center locations page describes its Northern Virginia presence as 400 plus MW across 142 acres in Manassas, and its own VA-1 and VA-2 solution guides separately describe an 83 acre campus that is the first of four planned campus data centers growing toward a nine facility, two million plus square foot development, confirming this is a real, large, multi building campus consistent with this registrys six separately numbered VA rows. This session resolved a street address for this specific VA-5 row. Reverse geocoding this rows own stored coordinates through a third party service returned 11580 Hayden Rd, Manassas, VA 20109 at 0.9 confidence, extending the same coherent, evenly spaced Hayden Rd numbering sequence, 11580, 11600, 11640, 11680, found across sibling VA rows in this same batch, treated here as the corroborating check in place of a named press or aggregator source, which this session did not find. reading.body:
Iron Mountain VA-5 is part of a multi-building campus in Manassas that the operator describes as 400 plus megawatts across 142 acres, organized as four planned campuses within a larger nine-facility development. The specific capacity of VA-5 itself is not published. If the 400 plus megawatts is distributed across four planned campuses, a rough estimate would be 100 megawatts per campus, which at typical AI training density of 40 kilowatts per rack would be roughly 2,500 racks. No certifications qualifying the campus for specific workloads are published.

Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities, of which 23 publish capacity figures totaling 1,375 megawatts. Iron Mountain's published Virginia capacity ranks 24th, below the threshold of published figures, though the operator's own statements place the Manassas campus within the state's significant infrastructure. Most facilities in Virginia publish no capacity at all.

The campus address is 11580 Hayden Rd, Manassas, VA 20109, resolved by reverse geocoding and corroborated by coherent address spacing across other facilities in the same campus cluster. Iron Mountain acquired its data center business in 2017 and operates it as part of a real estate investment trust, though the specific history of this Virginia location is not detailed in published sourcing. The operator's development plan confirms this is a substantive, long-term build-out rather than a single facility.
